# Tests {.unnumbered}

On this page we perform some tests:

- Check that equation macros render well in PDF and HTML (MathJax)
- Test some non-standard MathJax extensions
- Check that python runs well
- Check that a proper bibliography is generated
- Any other relevant test...

This page has to be commented in `_quarto.yml` for final production.


## Equation macros 


### Vectors and matrices

| macro         | result                 |
| ------------- | ---------------------- |
| `\mbc`        | $\mbc{E}$              |
| `\mathbfcal`  | $\mathbfcal{E}$        |
| `\mathcal`    | $\mathcal{E}$          |
| `\vb`         | $\vb{x}$               |
| `\vbh`        | $\vbh{x}$              |
| `\mat`        | $\mat{H}$              |
| `\op`         | $\op{L}$               |
| `\transpose`  | $\transpose{\mat{M}}$  |
| `\htranspose` | $\htranspose{\mat{M}}$ |
| `\tensoru`    | $\tensoru{r}$          |
| `\tensoruu`   | $\tensoruu{r}$         |
| `\tensoruuu`  | $\tensoruuu{r}$        |

## Chemical formula using `mhchem` package 

We love lithium niobate: $\ce{LiNbO3}$

Works with both PDF (`\usepackage[version=4]{mhchem}`) and HTML (with MathJax) outputs:

[https://docs.mathjax.org/en/v3.0/input/tex/extensions/mhchem.html](https://docs.mathjax.org/en/v3.0/input/tex/extensions/mhchem.html)


## Numbers + units using `siunitx` package

For HTML output, we use the MathJax extension [https://github.com/limefrogyank/siunitx-pcc](https://github.com/limefrogyank/siunitx-pcc)

$\qty{25}{\meter\per\second}$

## Python code / graphic 

We test the Matplotlib style sheet `physrev_mplstyle` to be used to generate Physical Review compatible plots. We directly use the example provided on the style sheet repository.

See [https://github.com/hosilva/physrev_mplstyle/tree/main](https://github.com/hosilva/physrev_mplstyle/tree/main).

```{python}
#| label: fig-test_matplotlib
#| fig-cap: "A simple line plot generated with Matplotlib."


import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

%matplotlib inline
%config InlineBackend.figure_format='retina'

plt.style.use('../physrev.mplstyle')
#plt.rcParams['figure.dpi'] = "200"

f, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1)

x = np.linspace(0, 1)
s = np.flip(np.arange(1, 1 + 9/10., 1/10))

for slope in s:
    ax.plot(x, slope * x, label="{:0.1f}".format(slope))

ax.set_xlim(0, 1);
ax.set_ylim(0, 2);

ax.set_xlabel(r'$x$')
ax.set_ylabel(r'$y = s \, x$')

ax.legend(ncol=3)
ax.get_legend().set_title(r"Values of $s$")  
ax.grid()

# For Mathematica default palette
# filename = 'example'

# For gnuplot default palette
# filename = 'example_gp'

# For README
# plt.savefig(filename + '.png', dpi=600) 

# For paper:
# plt.savefig(filename + '.pdf')
```


```{python}
#| label: fig-line-plot
#| fig-cap: "A simple line plot generated with Matplotlib."


#import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
#import numpy as np



x = np.linspace(0, 10, 100)
y = np.sin(x)

plt.plot(x, y)
plt.show()
```
